text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The state has agreed to provide a special guarantee to cover debts of the General Workers Union (UGT) trade union group.

- The privatisation of the port of Leixoes in northern Portugal has been postponed from this year to 1998 due to the cancellation of a public competition for bids. The port operators consider the postponement "extremely harmful."

- A study by the state-run National Statistics Institute (INE), based on data from the 1991 census, says that there is a narrower range of industries in northern Portugal than in the main cities of Lisbon and Oporto. Most of the active population is concentrated in coastal areas.

- A group of officials from state chemicals company Quimigal has asked the Administrative Supreme Court to suspend a decree-law authorising the privatisation of the company until a previous case brought by the group in May 1996 is resolved.
- Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco has told parliament that he would present a bill to reform the tax system by June.

- Economy Minister Augusto Mateus is expected to conclude an agreement with UTA - United Technologies Automobile in Detroit today for a seven billion escudo investment in a new factory in Povoa de Lanhoso in northern Portugal to manufacture car wiring.
- The 1996 consolidated net profit of state bank Caixa Geral de Depositos dropped 14.7 percent year-on-year to 49.8 billion escudos.
- According to the European Commission, Portuguese GDP rose 2.51 percent in 1996. Portugal was one of the three countries, with Greece and the Netherlands, to grow faster in 1996 than in 1995.
